task: Four anonymous Sumner Norman BCI chart marks: candidate recheck
scope: Local research artifacts only; no repo edits, outreach, external writes or source assignment claims.
important_new_check: Direct original image yields ~.93,.79,.16,.55, slightly above the supplied photograph digitization ~.90,.76,.16,.53. Neither is author printed data.
conversion_policy: Illustrative output-code equivalents only. Use same explicitly assumed log2(28) bits/character for comparison; do not call these author-reported bitrate, measured channel capacity, or proof of chart identity. A byte equivalent is 8 bits/character and is distinct.

records.preferred_candidate: Gilja et al. (2015), Clinical translation of a high-performance neural prosthesis
records.match_reason: Publication year and printed .93/.92 are close to the photograph and the direct original-image mark (~.929).
limitations: Fitts bits/s excludes hold time; it is not achieved grid bitrate.
No author-provided original chart data links this mark to Gilja.

alternatives.result: 0.93 bps for T6; 0.59 average across four
alternatives.source_basis: Printed retrospective Table 1 in Pandarinath et al. (2017), not an explicit .93 table recovered in the original 2015 paper.
alternatives.original_2015_formula: eBR = CSPM * log2(N-1) / 60, N=8, radial sessions only

records.preferred_candidate: Bacher et al. (2015 issue; online 2014), Neural point-and-click communication by a person with incomplete locked-in syndrome

source_reported_numbers.condition: quick fox task; word completion enabled

records.value_basis: native ccpm; bps is analyst-derived only

illustrative_conversion.assumption: Assume an equiprobable 28-symbol output alphabet; 28 is not asserted as the Radial Keyboard target count or its actual language entropy.

records.match_reason: Correct year (issue date) and cursor-controlled text entry; defensible coding-convention proxy yields .75-.83 bps, bracketing the direct original mark (~.788).
limitations: No primary author-reported .76 or .79-bps value found.
Prediction conditions differ; cannot treat 10.4 as prediction-free.
The Radial Keyboard uses ambiguous groups and disambiguation, so an output-character code must not be called measured command-channel bitrate.

alternatives.candidate: Gilja et al. (2015), full acquisition-time Fitts-style re-expression
alternatives.confidence: low; derived, not the authors printed score
alternatives.warning: Authors report .93/.92 after subtracting hold; .773/.768 are new analyst calculations. Do not infer two distinct studies from them.

records.preferred_candidate: Vansteensel et al. (2016), Fully Implanted Brain-Computer Interface in a Locked-In Patient with ALS
records.value_basis: native letter timing; bps is analyst-derived only

illustrative_conversion.assumption: Uses rounded headline and assumed uniform 28-symbol code, not measured ITR.

byte_equivalent_check.basis: 1 byte/letter; encoded payload equivalent, not neural-information bitrate

records.match_reason: Year and landmark implanted communication demonstration fit; rounded two-letter/minute result converts to ~.16 under explicit convention.
limitations: Subdural ECoG neural-click/scanning interface, not literal 2D cursor/grid control.
Actual 52/33-second timings give .092/.146 under the same 28-symbol convention, not .16.
Pandarinath 2017 reports .21 ITR in a separate column and leaves bitrate blank; cannot relabel .21 as the figure value.
